epic.title: program(runtime): Node/Bun compatibility layer for migrated mains — process facts, module specifiers, native addon policy, child_process broker, ecosystem packages
epic.body:
## Scope
Process-level Electron facts consumed at module evaluation (type, versions, defaultApp, resourcesPath, mas, windowsStore, sandboxed, contextIsolated), the five module specifiers (`electron`, `electron/main|renderer|common|utility`), native addon classes (better-sqlite3, nodehun, node-pty, keytar, sharp, @parcel/watcher; chokidar 5 is pure JS over fs.watch; fsevents transitive), strict vs legacy labelling, child_process replacement, and the ecosystem packages that wrap Electron (electron-store, electron-log, electron-context-menu).

## Design facts from research (NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2; decisions below stay open except where the panel settled them)
- Boot facts are host-minted at spawn and read synchronously at import (settled by the panel).
- Migrated apps start `unverified` (KEL-78 default) and the report prints it; `legacy` is written only when the user accepts the forfeit; every surface prints "legacy — zero-authority claim forfeited" (settled by the panel).
- Native addon policy follows KEL-78's four-outcome tree with a KEL-215-shaped evidence row per (version, OS/arch, Bun revision, artifact digest, operation); no in-process load under strict.
- child_process under strict is a host `process` broker row (KEL-76 owner) with a child_process-shaped facade conforming to KEL-77's five Node oracles; under legacy Bun's node:child_process with documented gaps.
- electron-store/electron-log/electron-context-menu are an aggregate oracle for the median main-process surface (candidate `package` panel).

verdicts.reason: The mechanism survives; the named owners and blockers do not. FACT: @keld/api reads only process.env.KELD_APP_LINK and all lifecycle state is async; @keld/electron installs only process.type and versions.electron at import. FACT: keld-runtime RoleConfig already has a per-generation env list, applied on the normal path and on the Linux strict exact-environment launch, so a host-minted facts value needs no new transport, no second link and no inherited handle. That matches the map's settled 'boot-static values synchronous at import'. Three sub-claims are wrong. (1) The evidence line '[fact] kel78: adding a bootstrap payload is a public-API/permission review gate item, not a wire change if delivered out-of-band' is not in the spec; it is an inference. What the specs say is the opposite direction: KEL-78 section 4 I/O 'The child receives KELD_APP_LINK and fixed-direction log sinks only', AC4 allows no extra inherited handle, and arch 06 section 1 says 'There are no parallel KELD_LINK, KELD_SHM or KELD_CONTRACT contracts'. A facts value is therefore an amendment to two stated contracts, and the 'inherited fd' option is excluded outright. (2) keld-pack ExpectedAppIdentity is not the owner of resourcesPath/appPath/isPackaged/name/version: its payload is exactly app_id, channel, target, update_public_key, and its decoder is Windows-only. (3) Both blockers are stale in live Linear: KEL-15 is Done (config RFC, last updated 2026-07-10) and KEL-19 is a Done CLI RFC whose live work is the Windows PE identity container (T1 landed, T2 Windows proof, T3 keld build gated).

verdicts.reason: The proposed single resolver owner does not work on the pinned Bun. FACT (executed, Bun 1.4.2 macOS arm64): a plugin registered through bunfig `preload` with onResolve filter /.*/ is called for the entry file and for relative specifiers, but never for bare `electron`, never for `electron/main|renderer|common|utility`, and never for `child_process`/`node:child_process`. This held for static ESM import (.mjs and .ts), dynamic import, CJS require, and a require inside a node_modules dependency. With a real `electron` in node_modules the app got the real package; with none, Bun auto-resolved `electron` to ~/.bun/install/cache/electron@44.5.1 and subpaths failed with 'Cannot find package'. The same onResolve does fire for bare specifiers inside Bun.build, so only the bundler half of the claim holds, and arch 06 section 2 says `keld build` uses the app's own bundler, so Keld owns no Bun.build call to attach it to. Second refuted sub-claim: 'tsconfig paths stays the editor/type mapping'. FACT: on Bun 1.4.2 tsconfig paths is a live runtime resolver that outranks node_modules for bare `electron`, in app code and in a node_modules CJS dependency, while subpaths still go to node_modules; Node ignores it. Keeping it beside any other alias gives two runtime owners and can load two module instances. Third: the decision duplicates X02-A1, which the published plan already names as the one alias owner. The alternative A2 never evaluated passes: a package.json dependency whose key is `electron` plus an exports map resolved all five specifiers for import and require, in app code and in a CJS dependency, on both Bun 1.4.2 and Node 26.10. That is also what arch 04 section 2 already says ('@keld/* deps replace electron*').

Linear KEL-76 independently supports 'load is not the oracle' (node-pty loaded under Bun but a real /bin/sh probe produced no data). What does not hold: (1) Scope. No corpus package.json contains better-sqlite3, keytar, node-pty, @parcel/watcher or sharp; Zettlr has only nodehun, chokidar ^5 and an optionalDependencies fsevents; draw.io has no native addon. KEL-127 lists 'additional native-module names' as a non-goal before G2, and G2 is not complete (KEL-140, KEL-141, KEL-143 Backlog; KEL-144 Backlog). Typing this a `task` and publishing X03-T2 as ready-for-agent runs ahead of that and of the first proof. (2) chokidar under strict is not a Bun fs.watch question: arch 05 `fs+` row already assigns watching to the host fs broker with a 'strict-profile virtual Node-fs/watcher facade'. A Bun fs.watch differential only describes the legacy path. (3) 'KEL-77 family extension' is not available as-is: the approved KEL-77 spec is one family with N-API and libuv as explicit non-goals, and Linear KEL-77 is a showcase lane 'not a Keld framework phase blocker'. A new family needs its own approved slice. (4) keytar to safeStorage over `secrets`: the MODULES row exists but two Linear searches found no owner issue (inference: none exists). Note for the owner: AC6 says there is no in-process option for untrusted native code without the 'under strict' qualifier that section 4 carries; the legacy in-process row rests on section 4 and on KEL-78's 'legacy as disclosed exception' text.

verdicts.reason: The rule is determined by existing owners and I could not break it. FACT: KEL-78 section 4 makes `unverified` the default, allows `legacy` only by an explicit Keld key, says 'Electron-compat apps do not silently start legacy', forbids auto-downgrade, and requires build/doctor/scoreboard/release surfaces to print the forfeit. admit.rs returns the three report strings and the cited fix text. Listing sandbox:false windows as a strict blocker is consistent with admit(): a leftover Electron sandbox-off while Strict is requested is UnexpectedGrant. KEL-127 decision 4 ('opt-in, visibly labeled existing legacy profile, never a silent downgrade') and its analyzer rule ('read-only, emits reviewable reversible changes only after authorization') match 'write the key only on user acceptance'. Scoring cannot blend profiles: every evidence record carries authority_profile and the scorer requires records to agree. The blockers are wrong. KEL-15 is Done and does not own the key; KEL-78 section 4 says the key 'does not exist today' and adding it is a permission-model plus public-API gate. KEL-19 does not own migrate: the CLI's reserved-verb table tracks migrate at KEL-17 (Done) and build/ext at KEL-19. One consequence the decision omits: the evidence schema has no `unverified` value (only strict_bun, sandboxed_addon_worker, legacy_sandbox_off, user_approved_tool_child), so an unverified migrated app can produce no scoreboard cell at all. The first proof therefore needs the explicit legacy key to exist, and no open Linear task names that key as its deliverable.

verdicts.reason: The direction is the spec's own, so it survives; one evidence fact is wrong and three atoms are missing. FACT: arch 05 already defines a `process` row ('scoped executable launch, env/stdio, child lifecycle') whose facade is 'strict-profile child_process/utilityProcess broker facades' and says KEL-76 must approve and ship real behavior for process and pty. Linear KEL-76 acceptance has the same grant shape ('Guard evaluates executable, args, cwd, env and principal before creating a PTY or child') and excludes 'a generic unrestricted child_process escape hatch', which matches the rejected `process.spawn: true`. fork mapping to KEL-75 roles matches arch 04 section 3.1. Wrong fact: draw.io's spawns are not Windows-only. The execFile at electron.js:4413 runs `fc-list` on every non-Windows platform, including macOS, and resolves an empty font list on error. Under the legacy first proof Bun's own execFile handles it, so the broker is not needed for that milestone and this decision is parked, but the strict draw.io spec will meet it. Missing atoms: (1) Reachability. The alias cannot deliver a child_process facade: a runtime plugin never sees `node:child_process` and a node_modules package named child_process does not shadow the builtin (probes). The only path I could make work is a preload that replaces the builtin's exports, which ESM named, default, namespace imports and CJS require all then observe on Bun 1.4.2. That is a second injection mechanism with no named owner. (2) Deputy. A host-launched tool child (pandoc) runs with the user's authority unless its own profile is specified; KEL-78's 'descendants: same profile' covers role descendants only, and KEL-78 in Linear requires a deputy-escalation negative control. (3) The evidence schema already has `user_approved_tool_child`; the decision should use it instead of leaving brokered launches unlabeled. Owner drift: Linear KEL-76 is titled and scoped as PTY/ConPTY, is in Backlog with no spec file, while arch 05 gives it the non-PTY process row too.

verdicts.reason: Refuted as written: there is no `package` panel and one cannot be added without forking a closed schema. FACT: keld.compat.denominator/v1 accepts `panel` only as product or showcase (parse_panel rejects anything else), and `kind` only as install, activation, primary_workflow or full_feature. research.summary: Cross-cutting runtime layer for migrated Electron main processes on Bun. Findings: (1) Electron resolves the five module specifiers (electron, electron/main, electron/renderer, electron/common, electron/utility) with one Module._resolveFilename patch to a single builtin and ships no package.json exports; Keld must do the same with ONE resolver owner — a Bun preload plugin (onResolve covers bare specifiers for both import and require) — because bunfig.toml has no [alias] key at all (architecture 04 §2 names a non-existent key; the KEL-72 fixture still writes it) and tsconfig paths is only verified for ESM import of bare `electron` on Bun 1.3.14 while CI now pins 1.4.2. (2) Process-level Electron facts (process.type/versions/defaultApp/resourcesPath/mas/windowsStore, app.getPath/getVersion/getName/isPackaged/getAppPath) are consumed synchronously at module-evaluation time by real apps (draw.io constructs electron-store at top level), so they must be host-minted and delivered at role spawn, not fetched over kipc after ready. (3) Native addon policy follows the KEL-78 four-outcome tree with no in-process load under strict: better-sqlite3 (N-API, KEL-215 qualified only for 13.0.3/Bun 1.4.2/win-x64), nodehun (N-API, node-gyp source build, imported as a raw .node file by Zettlr), node-pty (N-API 7, KEL-76 host pty row), keytar (N-API 3, archived → safeStorage over keld-native `secrets`), sharp and @parcel/watcher (N-API prebuilds → addon worker). chokidar 5 is pure JS over fs.watch — a Bun fs.watch differential (KEL-77 family extension), not addon policy; fsevents is only a transitive chokidar@3 optional in Zettlr's lock. (4) Both corpus apps spawn external executables; raw child_process stays never-listed under strict, so a scoped `process` broker (KEL-76) with KEL-77's five lifecycle oracles as conformance is on the critical path for Zettlr, while draw.io's spawns are Windows-only. (5) Profile labeling: Electron-compat apps start `unverified`, never silently `legacy`; migrate must write the explicit Keld profile key only on user acceptance and print the forfeit. (6) electron-store/electron-log/electron-context-menu are the cheapest aggregate oracle of the median main-process surface and should become an unmodified package panel in the corpus. Evidence is insufficient to state Bun 1.4.2 Node-API coverage or whether nodehun/node-pty load on it; prototypes are proposed.
